subject: Re: MedSys renewal — KMS attestation + capacity uplift coordination
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medsys.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medsys.com; tom.reynolds@medsys.com
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedSys renewal / KMS attestation and capacity uplift

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the renewal packet you shared last week. Procurement wants to move forward but we have two outstanding asks before legal signs: 1) a short KMS attestation that explains where keys are held and who has access (we need to present this to our security committee), and 2) confirmation of the quarterly capacity uplift process — we plan to increase committed units by ~30% in Q3 and need to ensure the private offer supports staggered invoice tranches.

Attached is a short internal template (PDF) and our procurement checklist. Can Redwood produce a one‑page KMS attestation and confirm whether the proposed staggered tranches are supported in the private offer? Also, is there any SLA delta if we add the extra capacity?

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement aims to circulate to finance/legal by Tue.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Director, Vendor Ops
MedSys Health

Attachments: medsys_procurement_checklist.pdf
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medsys.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSys renewal / KMS attestation and capacity uplift

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and David (billing) to confirm the Docs and invoice cadence. Quick points from the platform side: 

- KMS: we can provide an attestation describing key custody models. For your private deployment we support both customer‑managed KMS (customers bring their own KMS/HSM) and Redwood‑managed keys with customer‑facing audit logs. I’ll attach a draft attestation and an integration matrix for the KMS handoff.
- Capacity uplifts: private offers support staged tranches. We typically map tranches to invoice buckets; finance will confirm whether we can stagger billing across months in the same renewal window.
- SLA: adding capacity does not change base SLA, but certain burst/over‑commit tiers may have different latency backstops — we’ll flag any SLA exceptions in the amendment.

Next actions: Kimberly, can you review the attached private_offer_draft_v3.pdf and the KMS matrix and advise on required legal language for attestation? David, can you confirm billing tranche support and whether invoice dates can be split into 30/60/90 day buckets?

I’ll stand by for a DocuSign link if procurement prefers to sign once the attestation and invoice cadence are confirmed.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: private_offer_draft_v3.pdf; kms_integration_matrix.xlsx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai; Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medsys.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSys renewal / KMS attestation and capacity uplift

Sara / team — I reviewed the draft private offer. Notes for Procurement and MedSys legal: 

1) KMS attestation: we can provide a customer‑facing statement limited to technical behavior and controls (key residency, access controls, audit logs, and rotations). We cannot provide private internal operational runbooks. I’ve inserted language in the attached sla_change_request.docx that should satisfy most security committees — please review and flag anything missing.

2) Bill tranches: Redwood finance supports a 3‑tranche invoice (initial acceptance, midterm topup, final balancing) in a single renewal if the PO references the tranche schedule. David — please confirm if we can map the Q3 uplift (30%) to the middle tranche and prorate accordingly.

3) Capacity uplift & SLA: no SLA change required for committed capacity increases. If MedSys opts into burst credit (pay-as-you-go surge) we’ll document latency targets for surge in the amendment. 

If everyone agrees, I’ll prepare redlines to the private_offer_draft and the attestation for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_change_request.docx
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsys.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medsys.com>; procurement@medsys.com
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSys renewal / KMS attestation and capacity uplift

Kimberly / Priyom — thanks, that looks promising. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

- The security committee specifically wants confirmation of envelope encryption at rest and differential access between Redwood SOC team and MedSys key admins. The draft language looks ok but can you make the attestation explicit about "separation of duties" and the read‑only access pattern for audit logs?
- For the invoice tranches: can Redwood accept the following split? 50% at signing (acceptance), 30% at start of Q3 (topup), 20% final reconciliation at year end. If yes, please provide sample invoice dates so we can align POs.

Also, we’ll expect a DocuSign link with the redlined private offer and a separate attestation PDF that our security team can attach to the packet. Can you target end of day Friday for those two items? That would keep our legal review on schedule.

Cheers,
Tom Reynolds
Sr. Procurement Manager | MedSys Health
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsys.com>; Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medsys.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSys renewal / KMS attestation and capacity uplift

Tom / Sara — all good, appreciate the clear tranche split. Quick status: 

- Kimberly has agreed to the more explicit separation‑of‑duties language; I’ve asked her to finalize the attestation PDF with that phrasing (explicitly calls out envelope encryption, key residency, read‑only audit access for Redwood ops, and customer KMS admin rights).
- David confirmed billing can support 50/30/20 tranches and will provide sample invoice dates for the PO; he’ll attach the invoice cadence to the DocuSign packet.
- We’ll prepare two deliverables by EOD Friday: 1) attestation PDF for your security packet, and 2) redlined private offer + DocuSign envelope with tranche schedule and the SLA amendment.

Action items for MedSys: please confirm the target invoice dates you prefer for the 30% tranche in Q3 (e.g., 2028‑07‑01 or 2028‑08‑01 are both feasible). Once you confirm dates we’ll bake them into the DocuSign and send over.

I’ll follow up as soon as DocuSign is ready. Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
